## Summary

- The Host screen groups the same readings into Overview, Storage, PostgreSQL, and Services. A history chart names each sample and leaves a gap empty. A dash means the window has no observation. Services can be compared on one pair of time bounds. A service CPU figure is time in that evaluation step. Memory and swap still have no history series.
- `GET /host` `charts.cpu_modes` is the average per-core rate of each mode, `avg by (mode) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total[120s]))`, in CPU-seconds per second. Each mode averages only the cores that reported a rate for it. A mode with no rate stays absent. Guest modes stay on this chart and stay out of `tiles.cpu.busy_share`. `busy_share` is unchanged.
- The channel canvas can arrange a graph. Arrangement writes display positions. Notes stay where they are. Edges, container membership, node configuration, and graph settings stay as they are.
- A channel graph may include `layout` (`auto` or `manual`) and a node field `execution_order` (an integer from 0 through 9007199254740991). Omitting both leaves a legacy graph: placement stays manual, and ready siblings still run by smaller canvas y, then x. Stored versions and run snapshots are not rewritten.
- The first geometry edit of a legacy graph stores priorities taken from the current y, then x order and sets `layout.mode` to `manual`. Nodes that share a parent and the same coordinates take node-id order, and the canvas says that tie cannot be recovered. After the draft is saved, ready siblings that carry `execution_order` run before siblings that do not, by smaller priority, then node id, including inside a container body. An `auto` save fills a missing priority from that node's index in the submitted `nodes` array.

## Operator notes

- Upgrade from v0.8.0. v0.1.6 and v0.1.9 were tagged and are not installable. Do not install them.
- No new keys in `.env.example`. Leave the live `.env` in place. `REFRAQ_MONITOR_PASSWORD` stays required and URL-safe (no `@`, `:`, `/`, `%`, `?`, or `#`). `REFRAQ_PROMETHEUS_URL` stays optional and still defaults to `http://prometheus:9090`.
- Download `docker-compose.yaml` and `prometheus.yml` from this release and overwrite both. Replacing only the Compose file leaves Prometheus without a scrape file. Do not overwrite the live `.env`.
- Compose still mounts named volume `refraq_pg` at `/var/lib/postgresql`. Default PGDATA is `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`. A site already on that mount, including one upgraded through v0.1.10, v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.6.0, v0.6.1, v0.7.0, or v0.8.0, keeps its cluster. A site that only used the published v0.1.8 asset must still copy the anonymous-volume cluster onto `refraq_pg` before `up -d`, using the command in the v0.1.10 notes. Do not run `docker compose down -v`. Do not restore `/var/lib/postgresql/data`.
- Replace the files, then `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. API start runs no new Foundation Upgrade. The new image tag recreates `ensure-entity-db` (`restart: "no"`). That one-shot still prepares `entity_data`, `entity_access`, `acl`, `channel_dataset`, and `entity_change_log`. It does not delete Entity rows. `ensure-monitor-role` still aligns `refraq_monitor`. Worker and Beat stay on the api image tag.
- `host:read` is unchanged. `GET /host` still accepts only `hour`, `day`, and `retained`. The read still uses one end Instant for every query. It issues those queries one at a time on one HTTP client, each with a five-second timeout, and returns no partial tiles or charts. A failed query is still `503` `HOST_SERIES_UNAVAILABLE`. Callers that treated `charts.cpu_modes` as a sum across cores must read the new samples as a per-core average.
- A node `position` must be a finite number. Infinity and NaN are `422` `REQUEST_INVALID`. A legacy save that omits `layout` and `execution_order` stores neither. JSON `null` for either is `422` `REQUEST_INVALID`. An `auto` body may omit `position`; the stored coordinates are `{ "x": 0, "y": 0 }`. The server does not generate display geometry. Published versions are not migrated. A draft run and a published run both execute the graph they were given: y then x when `execution_order` is absent, and explicit priority when it is present. Node Sample lists ready ancestors in that same priority order. That list does not replay the engine's depth-first walk.
- Metadata MCP and Entity MCP tool arguments and tool-call results are unchanged. Webhook delivery is unchanged.
- This release adds no schema revision. An older image ignores stored `layout` and `execution_order` and orders ready siblings by canvas y then x.
